clue.text: Book date with lover, say? Memory's useful for that

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a lovers' meeting is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a tryst is a secret meeting arranged between lovers
RAM is computer memory; with the 's it gives RAMS
useful means handy

explanation.surface: Someone planning a romantic rendezvous hopes a good memory will help with the arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks TRYST as heard, spelt TRIST. Laurence Sterne's comic novel is the book defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne's eighteenth-century comic novel is a famous example of a book.

clue.text: Following Twain's lead, it's harsh describing golf as a long and tedious walk

indicators.note: the rest of the answer follows the first piece, so it comes after it
the lead of a word is its opening letter, here of the author's name
describing is used in the sense of drawing a line round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: harsh means rude
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Taking a cue from Mark Twain, a critic calls golf a good walk spoiled, a harsh verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means going around, so RUDE encloses G; T, the lead of Twain's, comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A weary, plodding march on foot is exactly the kind of walk this word denotes.

clue.text: Meal on the plane, prepared for specific type of jumbo

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a curry from a subcontinental restaurant, as in going out for one

indicators.note: prepared signals that the letters of the following words are made into something new

explanation.surface: Airline food is served on a jumbo jet, prepared for a particular aircraft type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbo' looks like a jumbo jet; it is an elephant. 'prepared' rearranges THE PLANE, set below the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo is a common nickname for any elephant, and the Asian kind is one specific variety.

clue.text: Come and go, with animation

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
up means lively or animated, as in being up and about

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cartoon character who comes and goes in a lively fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive or appear somewhere is the phrasal-verb sense, a straight synonym of come.

clue.text: Arguably more mature worker is source of corruption

parts.note: more grown-up could be called more adult, a comparative only arguably a real word
the ant is the crossword's stock worker, from the worker ant

explanation.surface: An older employee is blamed for corrupting the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arguably' admits that ADULTER, more adult, is a coined comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: An impurity added to food or drink debases it, so it is a source of corruption.

clue.text: See 1
First of headwords dictionary has for country dances

indicators.note: first of signals taking only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
has means owns

explanation.surface: A lexicographer checks what the dictionary lists first under country dances.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lively American folk gatherings with square dancing, so they are country dances.

clue.text: Offer from wicked sorcerer, possibly Mr Flood's pal

parts.note: read the phrase in the answer as an instruction: the first word is a signal to rearrange, and the remaining three words, run together and rearranged, spell these clue words

explanation.surface: A wicked sorcerer's proposal might be made to Mr Flood's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: 'possibly' tells you the answer is itself wordplay whose result is the clue's 'Mr Flood's pal'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Aladdin pantomime the disguised magician cries this swap offer to trick Aladdin's household out of the magic lamp.

clue.text: Having some spring produce in garden's front border

parts.note: to produce a crop is to yield

indicators.note: the front border of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A gardener talks about growing produce in the border at the front of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks seasonal beside 'garden'; it means springiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives under pressure has some bounce or elasticity, i.e. some spring.

clue.text: Charge less than Greek character returning with reduction (two-thirds off)

indicators.note: returning means the Greek letter is read backwards

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: taken as a loose signal that the trimmed word's letters are rearranged
two-thirds off the word means keeping two-thirds of its letters, dropping the final third

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed

explanation.surface: A price cut leaves a Greek returning with two-thirds knocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds off' keeps six of nine letters, REDUCT, rearranged to DERCUT; 'with' is a weak anagram signal, the only word free for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To undercut a rival is to sell at a lower price than they charge.

clue.text: Twice No.1 birdcall

parts.note: number one is a childish word for urination, also called a pee
the same meaning given a second time: another childish word for urination is wee

explanation.surface: A bird's call is repeated, as if it were twice top of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No.1' is nursery talk for urinating; 'Twice' asks for two different words with that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of the lapwing is imitated by this word, which also names the bird.

clue.text: Good friend of Mole enthrals you with one tip

indicators.note: enthrals is read as holding within, so the friend's name takes the other letters inside

parts.note: Ratty is Mole's friend in The Wind in the Willows
U is the text-speak spelling of you
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Mole's good friend charms you with a single piece of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty, the Water Rat in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows, holds U and I after RAT. 'tip' is money, not advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a small sum given for service, which is exactly a gratuity.

clue.text: Playwright Jack maybe falls in love with? Just the opposite

indicators.note: falls in suggests one thing dropping inside another
just the opposite reverses the stated arrangement, so the playing card holds the others rather than falling into them

parts.note: a jack is one example of a playing card
love is zero in tennis, a round O

explanation.surface: Does a man called Jack fall in love with a playwright? Rather, the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' turns the order round: CARD takes in O and W, not the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward wrote Private Lives and Blithe Spirit, so he is a playwright.

clue.text: Other half of Wisconsin's affected by surprising change in the US

indicators.note: affected means acted upon and altered, so the letters are rearranged
half of means only the first half of the state's name is used

explanation.surface: The other half of Wisconsin is hit by an unexpected change in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of WISCONSIN'S is WISCO; with OTHER, it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This American slang word means an unexpected reversal or swap, a surprising change.

clue.text: Warn pidgin changes tack in the US

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A language warning: pidgin English changes direction in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes tack' reads as an idiom; 'changes' is the signal and 'tack' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call this short flat-headed pin for pinning paper to a board a thumbtack or tack.

clue.text: Bear ought to eat root tops

parts.note: ought to means should

indicators.note: tops are the first letters, in a down clue the top of each word

explanation.surface: A bear should eat the tops of roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like an animal; it is the verb to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a burden or responsibility is to bear it.

clue.text: See 2
Grandfather clock? One that's long been in service

definitions.text: One that's long been in service

parts.note: a grandfather is an elderly man, so old
a clock is a timer

explanation.surface: A grandfather clock is a fixture that has served a household for years.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran who has served or stayed somewhere for many years is a long-serving hand.

clue.text: Portrait of upper body that could be a Goodman, Wiseman or Deighton?

definitions.meaning: a painting showing the sitter from the head to the waist

definitions.text: that could be a Goodman, Wiseman or Deighton
definitions.meaning: Len Goodman, Len Wiseman and Len Deighton share the first name Len, which is the first half of the six-letter word for extent

explanation.surface: Which subject sits for a portrait of the upper body: a Goodman, a Wiseman or a Deighton?
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: LEN is half of LENGTH. Len Goodman judged Strictly Come Dancing; Len Deighton writes spy novels; Len Wiseman directs films.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting showing the sitter from the head down to the waist is the art term for this portrait type.

clue.text: A time entering change in the US, with husband going bust?

indicators.note: entering means the two letters go inside the other piece
change signals the remaining letters are rearranged
going means departing, so the letter is removed

explanation.surface: A time of change in America, with a husband going broke.
explanation.walkthrough: THE US less H gives TEUS, rearranged to STUE, which A and T enter. 'bust' looks like 'broke'; it is a sculpture, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a sculpted head and shoulders, a partial form of a sculpted figure, hence the question mark.

clue.text: See 7
Small donkey owner, ultimately one ignoring health warnings

parts.note: moke is a British slang word for a donkey

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A small donkey's owner is the one ignoring health warnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigarette packets carry health warnings, and someone who lights up regardless ignores them.

clue.text: Ruth follows on horse, possibly difficult to control

indicators.note: follows means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a rider on horseback is said to be up
ruth is an old word for pity, as in ruthless

explanation.surface: Ruth rides behind someone on a horse that may be hard to control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a name; it is the old noun for compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-important and above their station resists authority, so is hard to manage.

clue.text: Where Tom in Paris potentially meets retired Muslim in North Africa?

definitions.text: Where Tom in Paris potentially meets retired Muslim in North Africa?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and the French word for cat is chat

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Moor is a Muslim of North-West African descent

explanation.surface: Where might a Parisian called Tom meet a retired North African Muslim?
explanation.walkthrough: The French CAT and a backward MOOR meet side by side, and the whole clue describes an online place where strangers meet.
explanation.definitionFit: An online forum where strangers exchange messages in real time is where unlikely people meet.

clue.text: Expression of dismay as French cop mislays info about Spain

indicators.note: about means going around, so the shortened word surrounds the letter
mislays means loses, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a gendarme is a French police officer
gen is British slang for information
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A French policeman is dismayed when he loses his files about Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: GENDARME loses GEN to give DARME, which goes 'about' E.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of mild dismay or surprise, like goodness me or oh dear.

clue.text: Go after pine used for ornamental design in wood

indicators.note: after means the first piece comes after the second

parts.note: to pine is to fret or worry
to go, of a machine, is to work

explanation.surface: Go and fetch the pine to make a decorative wooden pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like timber beside 'wood'; it is the verb to fret.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative openwork cut with a fine saw in thin wood is the craft term for this ornament.

clue.text: Former No.1 cause of red nose — extremely drunk, following this order?

parts.note: the order meant is the instruction the answer's own first word gives, to send something back

indicators.note: following the order means obeying it, so the letters are sent back and written backwards
extremely means the outer letters of the word are taken

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard

explanation.surface: Too much drink causes a red nose, as a doctor's orders might say.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is its own instruction: reverse RED + NE + SOT to get the last two words. The Elvis Presley hit was a UK number one in 1962.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley's 1962 song topped the UK chart, making it a former chart-topper.
